speaker: Doctor
text:
Can you describe where you notice the double vision most clearly, and do you experience any drooping of your eyelids?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Creatine Kinase
REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); NORMAL READINGS (Complete Blood Count, Creatine Kinase)

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That previous diagnosis of Tuberculosis does not align with your symptoms of double vision and fluctuating weakness; could you tell me if you ever have difficulty swallowing, slurred speech, or trouble breathing? REQUEST TEST: Thyroid function tests, Chest CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Thyroid function tests: NORMAL READINGS; Chest_CT: Findings: Normal, no thymoma or other masses detected.
